performance.note: Analytical roofline (PRD §16.2). Three efficiency tiers (pessimistic/expected/optimistic, §16.3). Decode is bandwidth-limited at batch 1 on this GPU. Per-request decode and step latency are single-stream; aggregate throughput is at the SLO batch of 34 per group × 1 replica(s), where continuous batching amortises the weight read across the batch (§18.2).

practicalCapacity.note: 3 — limited by KV memory at maximum context. Agent/user translation deferred to Phase 3 (requires agent duty cycle, §19).

reasons: KV cache rounded to 128-token vLLM blocks
TP sharding: KV and weights divided by tensor_parallel=1
confidence.primaryUncertainty: Analytical roofline with broad efficiency ranges; hypothetical quantization adds weight-load uncertainty (PRD §16.3/§33)

evidence.source: FP32 logits over vocabulary + sampling workspace

assumptions.description: M_available = M_physical * U with U from GPU memory utilization.

Runtime memory follows PRD §14: M_fixed + M_token × 8192 scheduled tokens + M_sequence × 256 running sequences, on the Balanced profile (typical deployment estimate). Coefficients are architecture-derived and await benchmark calibration (§17).

Per-sequence activation is reserved at max_num_seqs, not at the concurrency solved for: vLLM profiles at its configured maxima and subtracts the result before allocating KV blocks, so the reservation does not shrink under light load.
vLLM KV blocksize = 128 tokens; rounded within one block.
Capacity is the total the driver reports (nvidia-smi memory.total), not a conversion of the marketed GB figure — the two differ by 0.6-7.4% depending on how much NVIDIA overprovisioned the part.
Analytical roofline uses broad efficiency tiers (BW: 0.40/0.55/0.70, compute: 0.30/0.50/0.65) per PRD §16.3; values are ranges, not precise predictions.

SLO concurrency (§18.2) is the largest batch B where T_prefill + avg_output × T_step(B) ≤ target, times the DP replica count. T_step(B) reads weights once per step and scales only KV and activation traffic with B (continuous batching); MoE routed experts are weighted by 1 − (1 − k/E)^B. Duty cycle and burst factors (§19) are not applied yet.

C_memory takes the *minimum* of the average- and maximum-context concurrencies, i.e. it assumes every concurrent request may simultaneously occupy its maximum context. This is deliberately conservative; a mixed-length workload supports more.
Tensor parallelism is modelled as linear scaling of bandwidth and compute. NVLink/PCIe all-reduce latency between ranks is not subtracted, so multi-GPU TP figures are optimistic.

warnings: Hypothetical quantization — weights use a format not present in the checkpoint; treat as an estimate.

derivations.label: Physical VRAM per GPU
derivations.meaning: What the driver reports the card has, which is not the number on the box. NVIDIA overprovisions each part so it can retire bad memory cells over its service life, by ~0.6% on Ada-class cards and ~7% on HBM and GDDR7 ones, so no arithmetic gets you from the marketed figure to this one. It is read from the catalog, measured per SKU.
derivations.substitution:
B200 SXM 180 GB reports 183,359 MiB
= 192,265,846,784 bytes  (marketed as 180 GB)

derivations.label: Allocatable VRAM per GPU
derivations.meaning: How much of the card the inference engine is allowed to claim. The remainder is left to the driver and fragmentation headroom, so the engine never runs the card to its literal limit.
derivations.substitution:
179.06 GiB × 0.90
(U = memory utilization ceiling, B200 SXM 180 GB catalog default)

derivations.label: Checkpoint storage
derivations.meaning: On-disk size of the weights at the selected precision — what you would download. NVFP4 is not exactly half a byte per parameter: each group of weights carries an extra FP8 scale byte.
derivations.formula: M_checkpoint = sum over components of  N × bytes(P)  +  ceil(N / G) scale bytes for NVFP4
derivations.substitution:
embeddings               308.28M × 0.5 B (nvfp4) + 19.27M scale bytes = 0.161 GiB
  output head              308.28M × 0.5 B (nvfp4) + 19.27M scale bytes = 0.161 GiB
  attention projections      2.80B × 0.5 B (nvfp4) + 175.20M scale bytes = 1.468 GiB
  dense MLP                113.25M × 0.5 B (nvfp4) + 7.08M scale bytes = 0.05933 GiB
  routed experts           113.55B × 0.5 B (nvfp4) + 7.10B scale bytes = 59.48 GiB
  shared experts           443.55M × 0.5 B (nvfp4) + 27.72M scale bytes = 0.232 GiB
  routers                   36.97M × 2 B (bf16) = 0.06887 GiB
  norms                     310.3K × 2 B (bf16) = 0.00058 GiB
  total                    117.56B params                   61.64 GiB

derivations.label: Weights resident per GPU
derivations.meaning: VRAM the model parameters occupy once loaded. Larger than the checkpoint because the engine needs repack/dequantization buffers, and divided by TP because tensor parallelism splits the model across ranks.

derivations.label: Runtime memory per GPU
derivations.meaning: Everything the engine holds that is neither weights nor KV blocks: the CUDA context, allocator, compiled kernels, captured CUDA graphs and collective buffers, plus the transient activations of the widest scheduler step and the logits and sampling buffers for every running sequence. Held back before any KV cache is budgeted.
derivations.formula: M_runtime = M_fixed + M_token × N_scheduledTokens + M_sequence × N_runningSequences
derivations.substitution:
2.08 GiB fixed (B200 SXM 180 GB catalog reserve + CUDA graphs)
+ 144.00 KiB/token × 8,192 scheduled tokens = 1.12 GiB
+ 784.00 KiB/seq × 256 running sequences = 0.19 GiB
(Balanced profile, ×1.00)

derivations.label: Free for KV cache
derivations.meaning: What is left on each GPU after weights and runtime overhead. This is the entire budget available to hold conversation context for concurrent requests — it is what caps concurrency.

derivations.label: KV cache per sequence @ average context
derivations.meaning: Memory one in-flight request holds to keep its attention cache at the average context length. Every concurrent request pays this.
derivations.formula: KV_seq = 2 × H_kv × D_head × B_kv × (L_full × S + L_sliding × min(S, W)) / TP

derivations.label: KV cache per sequence @ maximum context
derivations.meaning: The same cost for a request that has filled the context window — the worst case a single request can cost.
derivations.formula: KV_seq = 2 × H_kv × D_head × B_kv × (L_full × S + L_sliding × min(S, W)) / TP

derivations.label: Concurrent requests @ avg context
derivations.meaning: How many requests fit in VRAM at once if each holds an average-length context. A pure memory limit — it ignores whether the GPU is fast enough to serve them within your latency target.
derivations.substitution:
floor( 91.82 GiB / 0.785 GiB )
= floor( 98,586,681,385 bytes / 843,055,104 bytes )
= 116 per replica × 1 replica(s)

derivations.label: Concurrent requests @ max context
derivations.meaning: The same count in the worst case, where every concurrent request has filled the full context window simultaneously. Usually much smaller — it is the floor under which the deployment cannot be starved.
derivations.substitution:
floor( 91.82 GiB / 24.04 GiB )
= floor( 98,586,681,385 bytes / 25,807,552,512 bytes )
= 3 per replica × 1 replica(s)

derivations.label: Comfortable active requests
derivations.meaning: The headline number: requests that can be in flight at the same time while still meeting your latency target. It is the tightest of the three limits — running out of memory and missing the SLO are both failures, so the smallest one governs.
derivations.formula: C_comfortable = min( C_memory(avg), C_memory(max), C_SLO )   [all cluster-wide]
derivations.substitution:
min( 116, 3, 34 )
  C_memory(avg) = 116 — memory at average context (116 per replica × 1)
  C_memory(max) = 3 — memory at full context (3 per replica × 1)
  C_SLO         = 34 — latency target of 10.0 s

derivations.label: FLOPs per token
derivations.meaning: Arithmetic one token costs on a forward pass. Sets the compute side of the roofline — the floor on latency even with infinite bandwidth.
derivations.formula: FLOPs/token = 2 × active_params + 4 × H_q × D_head × sum(L × S_eff)
derivations.substitution:
matmul     2 × 8.45B active params = 16.90B FLOPs
attention  4 × H_q × D_head × sum(layers × context) = 10.12B FLOPs
total                                             = 27.02B FLOPs

derivations.label: Step latency
derivations.meaning: Wall-clock time to emit one token for one request. The roofline takes whichever is slower — moving the bytes, or doing the arithmetic.
derivations.formula:
T_step(B) = max( Bytes_step(B) / (BW × eff_bw), B × FLOPs/token / (Compute × eff_c) )
where Bytes_step(B) = W_step(B) + B × (KV_seq + activations)
derivations.substitution:
at B = 1, expected tier (eff_bw = 55%, eff_c = 50%):
Bytes_step = 4.74 GiB weights + 804.00 MiB KV + 2.25 MiB activations = 5.53 GiB
t_bandwidth = 5.53 GiB / (8,000 GB/s × 1 rank(s) × 0.55) = 1.35 ms
t_compute   = 27.02B FLOPs / (4,000 TFLOPS × 1 rank(s) × 0.50) = 0.01 ms
max(...) → bandwidth-limited

derivations.label: Decode rate per request
derivations.meaning: Tokens per second a single request sees once it starts generating. This is the number a user experiences as typing speed.
derivations.substitution:
1 / 1.06 ms = 944 tok/s   (optimistic tier)
1 / 1.85 ms = 539 tok/s   (pessimistic tier)

derivations.label: Prefill rate
derivations.meaning: Tokens per second while reading the prompt. Much faster than decode because one weight read is amortised across the whole prompt, which usually leaves prefill compute-limited rather than bandwidth-limited.
derivations.formula: prefill_tps = min( BW × eff_bw / bytes_per_token , Compute × eff_c / FLOPs_per_token )
derivations.substitution:
bytes/token = 65.95 GiB weights / 32,768 ctx + 96.00 KiB KV write + 2.25 MiB activations
= 4.40 MiB
bandwidth-bound: 952682 tok/s   compute-bound: 74032 tok/s   (expected tier)

derivations.label: Time to first token
derivations.meaning: How long a request waits before the first token appears: read the whole prompt, then run one decode step.
derivations.substitution:
32,768 tokens / 96242 tok/s + 1.06 ms = 341.53 ms   (optimistic)
32,768 tokens / 44419 tok/s + 1.85 ms = 739.55 ms   (pessimistic)

derivations.label: SLO concurrency
derivations.meaning: The largest batch that still meets your latency target, times the number of independent replicas. Purely a speed limit — memory is accounted separately.
derivations.formula: C_SLO = DP × max{ B <= C_memory(avg) : T_prefill + N_out × T_step(B) <= target }
derivations.substitution:
T_prefill = 32,768 tokens / 74032 tok/s = 442.62 ms
at B = 34: 442.62 ms + 512 output × 18.62 ms = 9.97 s  <=  10.0 s target
C_SLO = 34 × 1 replica(s)

derivations.label: Aggregate decode throughput
derivations.meaning: Total tokens per second the whole deployment emits with every slot busy. Continuous batching reads the weights once per step and shares them across the batch, so this is far above one request's rate.
derivations.substitution:
34 / 14.63 ms × 1 replica(s) = 2325 tok/s   (optimistic)
34 / 25.60 ms × 1 replica(s) = 1328 tok/s   (pessimistic)
